name: Outdoor Stage Two-Person Showdown
description: Develops a character description, ability type, stage setting, or climax structure into an audience-POV outdoor stage showdown short between two performers, moving stage by stage through creative spec, storyboard, key elements, single-shot video, and audio layers.

planning.planning_notes: Dynamic path: first decide the entry from aspect_ratio, resolution, venue_type, vo_language, the user's character/ability description and the canvas assets. Before creating generation nodes, settle the creative spec at the Skill level: lock 15 seconds per video, one shot per video, two characters A/B, both abilities, stage blocking, the conflict between them, aspect ratio, resolution, outdoor-stage realism and the voiceover language; this spec does not create its own node. If the user gives only one character, first complete or propose a second original rival/partner; never make a solo ability showcase. After the spec, create the storyboard: each video has exactly 1 shot, written as Beat 1 → Beat 2 → Beat 3 → Beat 4 → Final beat escalating inside one continuous take, with no seconds and no hard cuts. After the storyboard, create the key element stage with a separate key element node for each independently referenced asset: Character A, Character B, the complete outdoor stage/theater space, key props, and each side's ability effect source; do not create an audience POV asset. Never merge several subjects into one key element sheet; only an asset always referenced downstream as one whole may share a node. After the key elements, create the single-shot videos; each 15-second video references the confirmed Character A, Character B, stage/scene and any needed props/effect sources; generate visuals only at first, without VO/BGM. After the visual videos, create the audio layer and generate the VO and BGM prompts in one pass. Finally create the composite node automatically and connect all single-shot videos and the audio layer in playback order; BGM defaults to 0.7, VO to 1.0, and each video fades out over its last 2 seconds.
planning.prompt_guide: The core is the audience's first-person view of a two-person supernatural performance/duel on an outdoor stage. The camera feels like an audience member's eyes or phone camera, but never shows the phone body, a recording UI, picture-in-picture or a large centered phone. By default it is not a professional camera position, drone, broadcast camera or third-person film shot. Each 15-second video is one continuous handheld long take; write the internal rhythm only as narrative beats, with no timestamps, no hard cut/switch angle/new shot. Characters must read as real stage actors/stunt performers: real body proportions, fabric folds, leather/metal/armor texture, props with weight. Abilities must be translated into stage lighting, smoke, fire rings, LED light curtains, light columns, shockwaves, projections and live post-production enhancement.
conduct_rules: Default to two characters A/B; if the user gives only one, complete or ask for a second original rival/partner. Never default to a solo ability show.

If the user mentions a famous anime/game character, use it only as inspiration; never write the official character name, title, move names, organization names, village names, catchphrases, emblems or patterns in the storyboard or prompts.
Each 15-second video is exactly 1 shot; escalate inside it with Beat 1/2/3/4/Final beat, without seconds and without splitting into multiple shots.

The key element stage must be split into several independent nodes, at least Element_Character_A, Element_Character_B and the complete stage space; each side's ability effect source, core props or special stage rigs that are referenced across shots must also get their own node. Audience POV is a shot constraint, not a separate asset.

Every shot uses three-layer composition: foreground audience heads/shoulders/arms and a little phone edge, midground stage and both characters, background outdoor theater architecture/light rigs/flags/sky/smoke layer.
Every Beat keeps the other character present as target, defender, reactor or spatial anchor; it must never become two separate showcases.
Hit feedback must be specific: center of gravity, footwork, face guard, sliding step, bent knees, bracing and recovering balance; effects never replace the body's reaction.
Audience reactions change by side: when A leads, A's supporters cheer; when B counters, the other side of the audience stands, raises hands and phones shake.
Video prompts default to no music and no subtitles; VO and BGM are generated separately only after the visual videos are done.

rating_bands.description: The two characters' stage relationship is clear, the audience-POV long take is stable, and three-layer composition, IP avoidance, stage effects, hit feedback, side-based audience reactions and stage boundaries are all complete.
Basically a stage duel, but character B, foreground audience, real stage texture, hit feedback, IP rewriting or staged audio handling has gaps.
Turned into a solo ability show, professional film camera positions, third-person shots, hard-cut multi-shot, official IP written directly, a centered phone screen recording or a pure CG arena.

visual_review_items.name: Audience POV
visual_review_items.description: The camera must feel like a live long take through an audience member's eyes/phone camera, without showing a recording device or UI.

visual_review_items.name: Two-character relationship
visual_review_items.description: A and B share one stage coordinate system; attack, defense, reactions and the climax happen between them.

visual_review_items.name: Live realism
visual_review_items.description: Foreground audience, stage architecture, lighting and smoke, prop materials and body impact reactions must all be believable.

text_review_items.name: Single-shot rule
text_review_items.description: Each 15-second video is exactly 1 shot, using narrative beats inside, with no timestamps or hard cuts.

text_review_items.name: IP avoidance
text_review_items.description: Famous characters must become original stage-performer designs, with official names, logos and moves removed.

text_review_items.name: Audio separation
text_review_items.description: The video stage generates no VO/BGM; short VO and instrumental/sound-effect BGM are generated after the visual videos are done.

domain_constraints: Never create an audience POV key element.
Never use official anime/game character names, move names, organization names, emblems or catchphrases.
Never show a large centered phone, recording UI, picture-in-picture, third-person film camera positions, drone shots, hard cuts or multi-shot switching.
